note: Catalog covering the solo-demonstrable capability space. Projects are tagged with capabilities from data/capabilities.json; a name not in that file scores zero silently, and a test guards against it. Capabilities marked 'outreach' or 'employment' in the vocabulary are never scored by the matcher, because no project can honestly evidence them.

projects.title: Price fifteen vendors in one software category and find the real decision rule
capabilities: Produce project documentation and decision logs
projects.artifact: A workbook with a live cost model, plus a written analysis
projects.dataSource: Vendor pricing pages, collected by hand with a date on every row

projects.title: Take one real feature from stakeholder request to tested requirement
projects.artifact: A traceability matrix, a story set with acceptance criteria, and a UAT plan
projects.dataSource: None needed. Use an open source project's real issue tracker as the stakeholder.

projects.title: Map a broken process end to end and cost the fix
capabilities: Map processes and build flow diagrams
Model current state, future state and the gap
projects.artifact: Current and future state flows, a gap register, and a costed recommendation
projects.dataSource: A process you can observe directly, at work or in a volunteer organization

projects.title: Run a full UAT cycle against someone else's software and report it
projects.artifact: A UAT plan, executed test cases, and a defect report with triage decisions
projects.dataSource: Any open source application with a public issue tracker

projects.title: Build an operational dashboard on a live public data feed
projects.artifact: A published interactive dashboard that refreshes
projects.dataSource: A public API with a history worth watching

projects.title: Audit a published dataset and document every defect you find
capabilities: Produce project documentation and decision logs
projects.artifact: A data quality report, a data dictionary, and the cleaning code
projects.dataSource: Any government or Kaggle dataset with known problems

projects.title: Measure whether a change actually changed anything
projects.artifact: A written analysis with the comparison group stated up front
projects.dataSource: A public before-and-after event with data either side

projects.title: Forecast something that matters and publish your error afterwards
capabilities: Run ad hoc analysis to answer business questions
projects.artifact: A forecast, the method, and a follow-up post scoring it against what happened
projects.dataSource: A public time series that keeps updating

projects.title: Write the full requirements package for a feature nobody has built
capabilities: Write functional specifications, BRD or FRD
Translate business needs into technical requirements
projects.artifact: An FRD, a story set with acceptance criteria, and a business rules register
projects.dataSource: A long-standing open source feature request with real discussion on it. The thread is your requirements input.

projects.title: Run a product backlog in public, and publish why you ordered it that way
capabilities: Prioritize a backlog or competing requests
Translate business needs into technical requirements
projects.artifact: A live public backlog, a written prioritization rationale, and a dated roadmap
projects.dataSource: A small tool you already own and real requests from its users

projects.title: Automate one manual job and document the before and after honestly
capabilities: Map processes and build flow diagrams
Model current state, future state and the gap
Produce project documentation and decision logs
projects.artifact: Current and future state flows, the working automation, and measured time saved
projects.dataSource: A repetitive task you actually perform, timed before and after

projects.title: Design a proper schema for a dataset published as a flat mess
projects.artifact: An entity model, a source-to-target mapping, a data dictionary, and the load code
projects.dataSource: Any government CSV release that should have been three tables and is one

projects.title: Join two public APIs that were never meant to meet, and spec the contract
capabilities: Translate business needs into technical requirements
projects.artifact: An integration spec with field mappings, error handling, and a reconciliation check
projects.dataSource: Two free public APIs with an entity in common and no shared identifier

projects.title: Write the same finding twice, once for engineers and once for the business
capabilities: Communicate to technical and non-technical audiences
Produce project documentation and decision logs
projects.artifact: Two write-ups of one analysis, published side by side, plus a note on what changed between them
projects.effort: a few days on top of an analysis you already did
projects.dataSource: Any analysis you have already finished

projects.title: Write the documentation a tool you use is missing
capabilities: Produce training materials and train users
Communicate to technical and non-technical audiences
Produce project documentation and decision logs
projects.artifact: A merged documentation pull request, or a published tutorial with a worked example
projects.dataSource: An open source tool whose docs you have personally struggled with

projects.title: Publish a dataset and govern it like it matters
capabilities: Produce project documentation and decision logs
projects.artifact: A published dataset with a field-level dictionary, a stated correction process, and versioning
projects.effort: 1 week on top of a dataset you built
projects.dataSource: A dataset you assembled yourself, with a date on every row

projects.title: Redo an analysis with a model in the loop and publish where it was wrong
capabilities: Use AI tools in the analysis workflow
Run ad hoc analysis to answer business questions
Produce project documentation and decision logs
projects.artifact: The analysis, a log of where the model helped, and a log of where it was confidently wrong
projects.effort: 1 week on top of an analysis you already did
projects.dataSource: An analysis you have already done by hand, so you have ground truth to check against
